verdict.reasoning: Patient reports painful urination: 'It hurts when I pee.' Duration confirmed: 'Uh, six days.'
Dysuria: 'It hurts when I pee.' Foul smell: 'I've got this very unpleasant smell that comes out.' Visible blood spots: 'I've had spotted, uh, blood in my urine. Spots.'
Location: 'In my lower tummy.' Midline: 'In the middle.' Severity: 'Seven.' Intermittent: 'Comes and goes.'

Denies fever and back/loin pain: 'No, not at all.' and doctor confirms 'you said you didn't have any lower back pain?... and no loin pain as well.' Denies vaginal discharge: 'No, just the blood spot.' However, appetite change is contradicted: patient says eating and drinking are fine ('have you been able to eat and drink OK? Patient: Yes.'), not that there was an appetite change.

First episode: 'Have you had these symptoms before? Patient: No.' No contributing factors: to exercise/dehydration/sexual activity — 'Have you been doing lots of exercise, been dehydrated, um, been having regular sexual intercourse or anything? Patient: No.'
'Have you had any problems with your kidneys, or any urine infections? Patient: I had IBS before.'
'Do you take that regularly? Patient: Yes.' 'And it, do you take it three times a day? Patient: Yes I do.' 'Two hundred milligrams? Patient: Yes.'
'Any allergies? Patient: Clindamycin.' 'You're allergic to Clindamycin, OK.'
'And anyone in your family had any medical problems? Patient: No.'
Living situation: 'Do you live with friends, family? Patient: I live with friends.' Job: 'And where do you work? What's your job? Patient: I'm a support worker.'
Alcohol: 'Do you drink alcohol at all? Patient: Occasionally.' 'So how much in a average week? Patient: One glass of wine a week.' Smoking: 'And do you smoke? Patient: No.'
Doctor states: 'it sounds very much like you, might have an infection in your urine.' There is no explicit mention of 'uncomplicated cystitis' or 'lower urinary tract infection' as diagnostic labels.
IBS is mentioned ('I had IBS before.' and Mebeverine use) but there is no explicit statement that IBS is 'stable' or commentary on its current control.

A 3‑day course of antibiotics is prescribed: 'It would just be for three days.' and 'the antibiotics, that I'm gonna prescribe.' However, the specific agent 'Nitrofurantoin or equivalent' is never named in the transcript.

'The other thing which is important to do is to drink, lots of water. So, two and a half to three litres a day.' and 'you can get some cranberry juice and take, drink that as well, that sometimes helps.'
'And also some, sachets um, which you can get from the chemist, some sachets which just help change the acidity of your urine.' This corresponds to OTC urine alkalinising sachets.

'Have you got a thermometer at home? Patient: No.' 'It would be helpful if you could get a thermometer from the pharmacy and, do check your temperature, just to make sure that it isn't, going up and down.'

Safety‑netting: 'if you feel like your pain is getting worse or not settling, you get lower back pain, um, or you're getting a high temperature, or you have any problems actually passing urine. Then it's very important that we speak to you again.' Also mentions recurrent problem: 'if it becomes a, common, thing or a recurrent problem. Then we need to talk to you again about it.'

'So, do I have to call after I finish my course of antibiotics. Doctor: No, not if you're better. If you're, if you feel like your symptoms get worse at any point, or they're not resolving with the treatment. Or you keep getting a similar, um, you keep getting a similar, problem, reccurently. Then it's important for us to talk, talk to you in more detail about that.' This indicates follow‑up only if symptoms persist, worsen, or recur.
